cues.text: Welcome to the light lab. You will fire a laser at different surfaces, test the laws of reflection, and then predict the images that curved mirrors make.
Let's start with flat surfaces. Pick a surface, predict what the laser beam will do, then fire.
Now the laws of reflection. Pick a law, predict where the reflected ray will go, then fire the laser.
Next, the rays you can draw on a curved mirror. Pick a ray, predict where it goes after it hits the mirror, then fire it.
Now the concave mirror. Slide the candle to a position, predict the image it makes, then trace the rays.
Same stand, new mirror: a convex one. Predict the image for each position of the candle.
Every experiment is run and explained. Check your table carefully, then lock it in.
Prediction locked. Fire when you are ready: the result is the only way to find out.
That is not what you predicted, and that is fine. Surprises are where the learning happens. Think about why.
Here are the textbook answers. Compare them with your table, and look again at anything that surprised you.
